title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 36 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 36.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 36, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jehoahaz was made king in Jerusalem
Jehoiakim was made king by the king of Egypt
The king of Egypt condemned the land in silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoahaz was made king in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:1 states that the people took Jehoahaz and made him king in Jerusalem first.

questions.question: How long did Jehoahaz reign in Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 36?
questions.correctAnswer: Three months
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:2 states Jehoahaz reigned three months in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who put Jehoahaz down as king in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:3 states the king of Egypt put Jehoahaz down at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What did the king of Egypt demand from the land after removing Jehoahaz?
options: One hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:3 states the king of Egypt condemned the land in an hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

questions.question: Who was made king over Judah and Jerusalem by the king of Egypt after Jehoahaz was removed?
options: Eliakim, whose name was changed to Jehoiakim
questions.correctAnswer: Eliakim, whose name was changed to Jehoiakim
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:4 states the king of Egypt made Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim.

questions.question: How old was Jehoiakim when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty-five years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:5 states Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: How many years did Jehoiakim reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Eleven years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:5 states Jehoiakim reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What is said about Jehoiakim's actions in the sight of the LORD?
options: He did that which was evil
He did right in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He did that which was evil
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:5 states Jehoiakim did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD his God.

questions.question: Who came against Jehoiakim to bind him in fetters and carry him to Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:6 states Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jehoiakim and bound him in fetters.

questions.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar do with the vessels of the house of the LORD?
options: Carried them to Babylon and put them in his temple
Gave them to the king of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Carried them to Babylon and put them in his temple
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:7 states Nebuchadnezzar carried the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon and put them in his temple.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 36, who reigned after Jehoiakim?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoiachin his son
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:8 states Jehoiachin his son reigned in Jehoiakim's stead.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoahaz was carried to Egypt by Necho after being removed as king.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:4 states Necho took Jehoahaz his brother and carried him to Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: The acts and abominations of Jehoiakim are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:8 states the rest of Jehoiakim's acts and abominations are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that Nebuchadnezzar destroyed the city of Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Nebuchadnezzar destroying the city; it only mentions him binding Jehoiakim and carrying off the vessels (2 Chronicles 36:6-7).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states that Jehoahaz reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:2 states Jehoahaz reigned three months, not eleven years.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Jehoiachin reign in Jerusalem before being taken to Babylon?
questions.correctAnswer: Three months and ten days
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:9 states Jehoiachin reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 36:15 promise will happen if people heed God's messengers, based on the command in 2 Chronicles 36:14?
options: The LORD will have compassion on his people and dwelling place
The people will be taken captive
The house of the LORD will be polluted
The wrath of the LORD will arise
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will have compassion on his people and dwelling place
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:14 commands not to transgress as the heathen did and pollute the house of the LORD, and 2 Chronicles 36:15 explains God sent messengers because He had compassion on His people and dwelling place.

questions.question: What was Zedekiah’s attitude toward the prophet Jeremiah’s warnings?
options: He ignored Jeremiah and hardened his heart
questions.correctAnswer: He ignored Jeremiah and hardened his heart
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:12-13 shows Zedekiah did evil, did not humble himself before Jeremiah, and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD.

questions.question: How did the people's actions contribute to the LORD's wrath, based on 2 Chronicles 36:14 and 2 Chronicles 36:16?
options: They transgressed and mocked God’s messengers
They built altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They transgressed and mocked God’s messengers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:14 records their transgressions polluting the LORD's house, and 2 Chronicles 36:16 states they mocked God's messengers until the LORD's wrath arose.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience can be learned from Zedekiah’s rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar?
options: Disobedience leads to hardening of the heart and consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to hardening of the heart and consequences
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:13 shows Zedekiah rebelled and hardened his heart, illustrating how disobedience leads to spiritual stubbornness and negative outcomes.

questions.question: What does the treatment of God's messengers in verse 16 teach about responding to correction?
options: Mocking and despising leads to God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Mocking and despising leads to God's wrath
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:16 records that mocking and despising God's messengers led to the LORD's wrath against His people.

questions.question: How does the LORD’s sending of messengers as described in verse 15 reflect His character?
options: He is quick to anger without warning
questions.correctAnswer: He is compassionate and patient
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:15 shows God sent messengers early and often because of His compassion for His people and His dwelling place.

questions.question: In what way does Zedekiah’s failure to humble himself before Jeremiah serve as a warning for Christian living?
options: Ignoring godly counsel can harden the heart and lead to ruin
Rebellion is a sign of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring godly counsel can harden the heart and lead to ruin
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:12 describes Zedekiah not humbling himself before Jeremiah, showing the danger of rejecting godly guidance.

questions.question: What is the consequence highlighted by the narrative when leaders and people transgress greatly as in verse 14?
options: The house of the LORD becomes polluted
questions.correctAnswer: The house of the LORD becomes polluted
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:14 states that the chief priests and people transgressed greatly and polluted the LORD's house.

questions.question: How does the captivity of Jehoiachin illustrate the importance of righteous leadership?
options: Evil leadership leads to loss and exile
Reigning at a young age prevents sin
questions.correctAnswer: Evil leadership leads to loss and exile
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:9-10 shows Jehoiachin did evil and was taken captive to Babylon, illustrating the consequences of unrighteous leadership.

questions.question: Why is it significant that Nebuchadnezzar took the goodly vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon?
options: It symbolizes the captivity and desecration of the temple
It was a gift to the temple in Babylon
It showed respect for Israel's God
It was a loan to be returned
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the captivity and desecration of the temple
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:10-11 describes Nebuchadnezzar taking the temple vessels to Babylon, symbolizing the exile and judgment on Judah.

questions.question: How can believers apply the example of the people mocking God’s messengers in verse 16 today?
options: By listening respectfully to correction and not despising godly counsel
questions.correctAnswer: By listening respectfully to correction and not despising godly counsel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:16 warns that mocking God’s messengers brings wrath, encouraging believers to receive correction humbly.

questions.question: What lesson about prayer and repentance can be drawn from the repeated sending of messengers in verse 15?
options: God patiently calls for repentance through His messengers
God does not communicate with His people
questions.correctAnswer: God patiently calls for repentance through His messengers
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:15 shows God sending messengers repeatedly because of compassion, demonstrating His patient call to repentance.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign and did evil in the sight of the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 36.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:5 states that Jehoiakim was twenty-five when he began to reign and did evil in the sight of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Judah repented after God sent messengers to warn them, preventing His wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:16 explains the people mocked and despised God’s messengers until the LORD’s wrath arose, showing they did not repent.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 36.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 36:17, who did God bring upon the people that slew their young men in the house of their sanctuary?
questions.correctAnswer: The king of the Chaldees
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:17 states, 'Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary...'

questions.question: What items were taken to Babylon as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 36:18?
options: All the vessels of the house of God, treasures of the house of the LORD, and treasures of the king and princes
Only the vessels of the house of God
The treasures of the king of Egypt
The sacred scrolls and the Ark of the Covenant
questions.correctAnswer: All the vessels of the house of God, treasures of the house of the LORD, and treasures of the king and princes
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:18 says, 'And all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king, and of his princes; all these he brought to Babylon.'

questions.question: What happened to the house of God and Jerusalem according to 2 Chronicles 36:19?
options: They burnt the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, burnt all the palaces, and destroyed the goodly vessels
They rebuilt the house of God and fortified the wall of Jerusalem
They placed guards around the house of God and palaces
They left the house of God and Jerusalem intact
questions.correctAnswer: They burnt the house of God, broke down the wall of Jerusalem, burnt all the palaces, and destroyed the goodly vessels
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:19 states, 'And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof.'

questions.question: How long did the people remain servants in Babylon according to 2 Chronicles 36:20?
options: Until the reign of the kingdom of Persia
Until the reign of King Nebuchadnezzar
questions.correctAnswer: Until the reign of the kingdom of Persia
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:20 says, 'And them that had escaped from the sword carried he away to Babylon; where they were servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia.'

questions.question: What was the purpose of the land remaining desolate for seventy years as stated in 2 Chronicles 36:21?
options: To fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, allowing the land to enjoy its sabbaths
To punish the people for their sins
To prepare the land for a new king
To allow the Babylonians to settle the land
questions.correctAnswer: To fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, allowing the land to enjoy its sabbaths
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:21 states, 'To fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.'

questions.question: What action did Cyrus king of Persia take in 2 Chronicles 36:22 to fulfill the word of the LORD?
options: He made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and put it in writing
He rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem immediately
He destroyed the temple in Babylon
He exiled more Israelites to Persia
questions.correctAnswer: He made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and put it in writing
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:22 says, 'Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia... the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing.'

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'sabbath' (שַׁבָּת) as used in 2 Chronicles 36:21?
options: A period of rest or cessation
questions.correctAnswer: A period of rest or cessation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'sabbath' (שַׁבָּת) in 2 Chronicles 36:21 refers to a 'period of rest or cessation,' signifying the land's rest during its desolation to fulfill God's command through Jeremiah.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in 2 Chronicles 36:17 with the phrase 'he gave them all into his hand'?
questions.correctAnswer: Metonymy
questions.explanation: The phrase 'he gave them all into his hand' in 2 Chronicles 36:17 uses metonymy, where 'hand' represents power or control over the people.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also prophesies the seventy years of desolation mentioned in 2 Chronicles 36:21?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 25:11
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 25:11 prophesies the seventy years of desolation, directly connecting with the fulfillment mentioned in 2 Chronicles 36:21.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God raising up a foreign king to accomplish His purposes as seen in 2 Chronicles 36:22-23?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 17:26
questions.explanation: Acts 17:26 refers to God determining the times and boundaries of nations, echoing the theme in 2 Chronicles 36:22-23 where God stirs the spirit of Cyrus to fulfill His word.

questions.question: What event directly precedes the proclamation of Cyrus king of Persia in 2 Chronicles 36:22?
options: The land remaining desolate for seventy years
The burning of the house of God
The carrying away of vessels to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The land remaining desolate for seventy years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:21 describes the land's seventy years of desolation, which immediately precedes the proclamation of Cyrus in verse 22.

questions.question: In the historical context of 2 Chronicles 36, what was the significance of the vessels taken to Babylon (2 Chronicles 36:18) in relation to the temple's holiness?
options: They symbolized the removal of God's presence from Jerusalem
They were used as trophies in Babylonian festivals
They were sold to pay tribute to Egypt
They were hidden by the priests before the exile
questions.correctAnswer: They symbolized the removal of God's presence from Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Taking the vessels of the temple to Babylon as recorded in 2 Chronicles 36:18 symbolized the loss of the temple's holiness and God's presence due to the people's rebellion and unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What typology can be seen in Cyrus’ proclamation in 2 Chronicles 36:23 concerning the building of God's house?
options: Cyrus as a messianic type foreshadowing Christ as builder of God's spiritual temple
Cyrus as a symbol of worldly conquest without divine purpose
Cyrus as a type of the Antichrist
questions.correctAnswer: Cyrus as a messianic type foreshadowing Christ as builder of God's spiritual temple
questions.explanation: Cyrus’ role in 2 Chronicles 36:23 as one charged by God to build His house serves as a typology foreshadowing Christ, the ultimate builder of God's spiritual temple.

questions.question: How does the parallelism in 2 Chronicles 36:19 emphasize the destruction of Jerusalem?
options: By listing the burning of the house of God, breaking down the wall, burning palaces, and destroying vessels in a series
By repeating the same phrase twice
By contrasting the good and bad deeds of the kings
By using metaphorical language about fire
questions.correctAnswer: By listing the burning of the house of God, breaking down the wall, burning palaces, and destroying vessels in a series
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:19 uses parallelism in listing multiple destructive actions to emphasize the thorough devastation of Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 36:17, the king of the Chaldees showed compassion to the young and old during the conquest.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:17 explicitly states that the king of the Chaldees 'had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age.'

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 36:15 teach about God's nature?
options: God's compassion and mercy toward His people
God's exclusive focus on foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: God's compassion and mercy toward His people
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 36:15 states that the LORD sent messengers early and often because He had compassion on His people and His dwelling place, showing God's merciful nature.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 36:16 teach about human sin and divine response?
options: Persistent rejection of God's messengers leads to inevitable wrath
God overlooks repeated offenses without consequence
Human sin has no effect on divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent rejection of God's messengers leads to inevitable wrath
questions.explanation: Verse 16 explains that the people mocked and despised God's messengers until the wrath of the LORD arose against them, indicating consequences for persistent sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 36:21 teach about divine providence and the Sabbath principle?
options: God fulfills prophetic timing for land rest through exile
The Sabbath is only a weekly moral obligation
Exile was unrelated to any divine command
The land's desolation was accidental, not purposeful
questions.correctAnswer: God fulfills prophetic timing for land rest through exile
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states the exile fulfilled the word of the LORD regarding the land keeping its sabbath rest for seventy years, affirming God's providential control over history and Sabbath observance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 36:23 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 23 shows that Cyrus acknowledges that all kingdoms belong to the LORD God of heaven, demonstrating God's sovereign rule over earthly kingdoms.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 36:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: In verse 17, the LORD brings the king of the Chaldees to punish the people for their sins, demonstrating God's attribute of justice in executing judgment.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 36:22–23 connect to the broader biblical theme of restoration?
options: It marks the beginning of Israel's return from exile under divine direction
It signals the permanent end of Israel as a people
It shows God abandoning His covenant promises
It emphasizes political independence without God
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the beginning of Israel's return from exile under divine direction
questions.explanation: These verses describe Cyrus being stirred by God to issue a decree allowing the Israelites to return and rebuild the temple, initiating restoration per God's promise.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 36:6–7 prepare the theme of Babylonian captivity in the Old Testament narrative?
options: They show the start of Babylon's judgment by removing the king and sacred vessels
They depict Israel's military victory over Babylon
They describe Babylon's destruction by Egypt
They focus on Israel's repentance and immediate restoration
questions.correctAnswer: They show the start of Babylon's judgment by removing the king and sacred vessels
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 recount Nebuchadnezzar binding Jehoiakim and taking temple vessels to Babylon, initiating captivity and demonstrating God's judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 36:12 and 36:13 teach about human rebellion and divine authority?
options: Human stubbornness against God's prophets leads to rebellion against God's sovereign agents
Rebellion is excused if done against foreign rulers
Divine authority is only symbolic without real consequences
Prophetic warnings are optional for kings
questions.correctAnswer: Human stubbornness against God's prophets leads to rebellion against God's sovereign agents
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows Zedekiah ignoring Jeremiah, and verse 13 shows his rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar, illustrating the link between rejecting God’s word and opposing His appointed authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 36:18 and 36:19 teach about the consequences of sin on sacred spaces?
options: Sin results in destruction and desecration of God's holy temple and city
Sin leads to increased blessings on the temple
The temple remains untouched despite sin
God's presence abandons the temple but protects the city
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in destruction and desecration of God's holy temple and city
questions.explanation: Verse 18 describes the removal of temple vessels, and verse 19 recounts the burning of the temple and city walls, showing the consequences of Israel's sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 36:4 and 36:10 teach about God's sovereignty over kings and kingdoms?
options: God raises and removes kings according to His sovereign will
Kings reign independently of God's control
God only blesses kings who are Israelites
Foreign kings are excluded from God’s plans
questions.correctAnswer: God raises and removes kings according to His sovereign will
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows Egypt removing Jehoahaz and appointing Jehoiakim, while verse 10 shows Nebuchadnezzar replacing Jehoiachin with Zedekiah, evidencing God's control over rulers.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 36:16–17 teaches that God is unjust by punishing innocent people. What does 2 Chronicles 36:16–17 actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is a righteous response to persistent sin and rejection of His messengers
God is indifferent to sin and its consequences
God punishes only the guilty individuals without communal impact
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is a righteous response to persistent sin and rejection of His messengers
questions.explanation: Verses 16–17 explain that the people’s mockery of messengers led to God’s wrath and just punishment through the king of the Chaldees, showing righteous divine justice.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 36:3 teach about human political powers under God's providence?
options: Even foreign kings act as instruments under God's sovereign control
Human political powers act entirely independently of God
God only uses Israelite kings for His purposes
Political power is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Even foreign kings act as instruments under God's sovereign control
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows the king of Egypt deposing Jehoahaz and exacting tribute, implying that God sovereignly uses foreign powers to accomplish His purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 36:15 specifically demonstrate regarding God's interaction with Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes how God sent messengers repeatedly and early because of His compassion, demonstrating His longsuffering patience despite Israel’s sin.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 36:20 connect the Babylonian exile to the wider biblical theme of covenantal discipline?
options: It shows exile as covenantal punishment until a divinely appointed time
It portrays exile as accidental and unrelated to covenant
It emphasizes Israel’s immediate restoration without discipline
It indicates that exile led to permanent loss of covenant status
questions.correctAnswer: It shows exile as covenantal punishment until a divinely appointed time
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states the exiles were servants in Babylon until Persia's reign, implying the exile was a divinely set period of discipline in covenant context.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 36:8 and 36:9 teach about royal responsibility and sin?
options: Kings bear responsibility for evil before God regardless of age or reign length
Young kings are exempt from divine judgment
Royal sin has no impact on the nation
questions.correctAnswer: Kings bear responsibility for evil before God regardless of age or reign length
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 describe Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin doing evil in the Lord’s sight, showing that even young kings are accountable for sin.
